claim: Current public global sources can quantify selected health-care-facility WASH service levels and define facility-audit and improvement methods, but do not yet provide a current, comparable measure of continuously available water and hand hygiene at primary-care facilities across low- and middle-income countries with facility frames, point-of-care observations, quality or quantity, repair or stock-out, and missingness fields.
failure_modes: A reader treats the JMP no-service estimate as a current primary-care facility denominator or as proof that every person served by a facility experiences the same failure.
A reader treats an improved or on-premises water source as safe, sufficient, continuously available, or functional at every point of care.
A reader combines HHFA, SARA, SPA, WASH FIT, and JMP fields without reconciling facility frames, observation windows, definitions, or missingness.
A reader uses WASH FIT score changes or facility observations as proof of reduced infections, mortality, or improved clinical quality.
A reader uses missing or refused facility records to rank, punish, exclude, or deprioritize facilities, workers, patients, or communities.
A policymaker treats the data-sufficiency claim as proof that a compatible national or proprietary facility dataset does not exist and skips a local data-owner search.
kill_condition: A public or authorized-for-analysis dataset is identified that covers at least 10 low- or middle-income countries with a reconstructable primary-care facility frame, standardized water and hand-hygiene definitions, repeated or explicitly time-windowed availability observations, point-of-care fields, relevant quality or quantity measures, repair or stock-out states, and documented missingness.
limitations: This claim concerns the public evidence architecture reviewed here, not the true global prevalence of unsafe or unavailable WASH services.
The reviewed sources do not include every national, proprietary, unpublished, or non-English facility dataset.
The distinction between primary-care and other health-care facilities is not consistently available in global sources.
A future release, data request, or country-specific search could falsify the claim without changing the underlying service problem.
